title: Former Costa Mesa Police Officer Pleads Guilty to Contacting His Mistress Thousands of Times Through Text, Phone Calls, and Social Media Messages, Including More than 100 Times in a Day, Illegally Accessing Confidential Law Enforcement Databases to Track Romantic Rivals, Ex-girlfriend, and Wife

reports.title: Former Costa Mesa Police Officer Pleads Guilty to Contacting His Mistress Thousands of Times Through Text, Phone Calls, and Social Media Messages, Including More than 100 Times in a Day, Illegally Accessing Confidential Law Enforcement Databases to Track Romantic Rivals, Ex-girlfriend, and Wife

summary:
Robert Jay Josett, 35, a former Costa Mesa police officer, pleaded guilty to three misdemeanors, unauthorized computer access and fraud, annoying and repeated phone calls, and contempt of court for violating a restraining order. Over nine months, he contacted his mistress thousands of times by text, calls, and social media, sometimes more than 100 times a day, threatened to reveal explicit photos, and demanded to know if she was with someone else. He also used law enforcement databases to track her, her romantic interests, and his wife.

Between June and December 2023, Josett made 13 CLETS inquiries not related to his job and used the FLOCK license plate reader system to track vehicles. After being placed on leave in December 2023, he accessed FLOCK in June 2024, to find her new boyfriend's address in Torrance. He was served with an emergency protective order and termination notice on June 28, 2024, then drove by her home and was arrested. He was sentenced to three years informal probation and a 52 week domestic violence program, and his POST certification review is pending.
